One of three conditions will result when a system of equations is solved by graphing.
We have already seen the first condition when the lines intersect. The point of intersection is the solution to the system.
The system of equations is called consistent for this condition.
Two lines will intersect at exactly one point whenever the slope of one line is different from the slope of the other.

DEFINITION
SLOPE - Recall the slope-intercept form, Y = mX + b where m is the slope and b is the Y-intercept. Rewriting the equations into this form shows that the slopes of lines are different.
If the lines are parallel then they will not intersect and there is no solution to the system of equations.
The system of equations is called inconsistent for this condition.no solution to the system of equations.
Parallel lines have the same slopes but different Y-intercepts.
Parallel lines have the same slopes but different Y-intercepts.
DEFINITION
SLOPES - Recall the slope-intercept form, Y=mX+b where m is the slope and b is the Y-intercept. Rewriting the equations into this form shows that the slopes of lines are the same.
The third condition results when one line is graphed directly on top of another. The slope and Y-intercepts are the same.
Since coinciding lines intersect at many points, there are an infinite number of solutions. The system of equations is dependent.
Dependent systems of equations have coefficient values that are multiples of each other.

The purpose of the addition method is to eliminate one of the variables by adding the equations together.
DISCUSSION
Let's see how this system of equations is solved by addition.
The addition method is based on the Addition Property......
ADDITION PROPERTY - The addition property states that adding the same quantities to both sides of an equation does not change the equality of the equation.
DEFINITION
Adding the two equations eliminates the Y variable because they have opposite signs.
The result is an equation with only one variable, X.
Substitute the X value into either one of the original equations to find the Y value.
